attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his co-authored post, in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: A fair present-tense observation. The draft drops two of the listed examples (question answering, cross-examination), but these were illustrations, so the core commitment is unchanged. The contract still lists them.

contract.note: The plain reading of competence as 'ordinarily usable, substantially correct work' is ordinary and fair. Judging each example separately and limiting the window to systems available by the post date are both reasonable.

evidence.note: Version available before the post. With human checking, ChatGPT scored a FActScore of 58% on biographies, which supports the factual-prose example only.
Human evaluation before the post: raters preferred LLM summaries to human-written ones, and the LLM summaries were more factually consistent. This contradicts including summarization.
Shows weaknesses in long-context retrieval and multi-document QA. It does not test whole-book understanding or set a human baseline.

reviews.rationale: Factual prose is supported: substantial unsupported content in ChatGPT biographies (e1). Summarization is contradicted: humans preferred LLM summaries (e2). Question answering, fact-checking, cross-examination and full-book comprehension are not settled; e3 is context only. The contract's 'several activities' support condition is not met, and one named example is contradicted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own co-authored words, reused from his earlier post and endorsed here.

semantics.note: Keeps the categorical inability claims for counting and multiplication, 'reliably' for kinship and chess, the biography/story scope, and the 'yet to see' framing for driving.

contract.note: Reading 'they' as contemporary LLMs, fine-tuned ones included, is ordinary; it cannot mean calculators. Scoring each component separately fits the bundled wording.

evidence.note: Many unsupported facts in generated biographies support the 'make stuff up' component for biographies.
Asymmetry on reversed parent–child questions (79% vs 33%) supports a specific failure to generalize kinship reliably.
Fine-tuned Goat-7B scored 96.7% on five-digit multiplication, against GPT-4's 0%. This contradicts the categorical claim that LLMs cannot do it.
GPT-3.5-instruct had a low illegal-move rate but validation was flagged as incomplete. GPT-4 often lost on illegal moves. Not decisive either way.
Waymo safety in its restricted operating domain. A specialized non-LLM system, so it cannot settle the claim.

reviews.rationale: Supported: biography fabrication (e1) and unreliable kinship generalization (e2). Contradicted: the flat claim that five-digit multiplication is impossible, since a fine-tuned LLM reached 96.7% (e3). Not settled by the packet: counting, chess-rule reliability (e4 is mixed context) and driving (e5 is out of scope).

semantics.note: The draft sentence leaves out image interpretation and reasoning, but the condition field and the contract keep the full list. The observation kind is correct.

contract.note: Counting vision transformers and hybrid systems as transformer use, and judging each area separately, is a fair ordinary reading of 'little to no use of the transformer architecture'.

evidence.note: In July 2023, DeepMind treated the transformer-based RT-1 as a state-of-the-art robotics policy. That is material transformer use in robotics.
DINOv2, a leading visual-feature model from April 2023, is built on ViT backbones. This contradicts the image-interpretation example.
The 2023 IPC optimal-track winner combines classical search planners with no transformer, which supports the planning example. The abstract's later analysis does not change the system's architecture.
Official results confirm Ragnarok as the winner, announced July 11, 2023.

reviews.rationale: Planning is supported: the 2023 IPC winner used classical search (e3, e4). Robotics and image interpretation are contradicted: leading systems used transformers centrally (e1, e2). Game playing, scientific applications and reasoning were not assessed and remain unresolved.
